AccountOut.description: Everything stored about an account (the rules too). Mirrors `accounts.Account`.
AccountOut.title: AccountOut

AccountProgressOut.description: How an account is doing against its rules, worked out from its closed trades.
AccountProgressOut.title: AccountProgressOut

AccountRulesIn.description: A rule left null is not tracked for the account.
AccountRulesIn.title: AccountRulesIn

BusinessTotalsOut.description: Across every account, archived ones included: is the prop business itself profitable?
BusinessTotalsOut.title: BusinessTotalsOut

FillPairOut.description: One row of the broker's export: a buy fill matched to a sell fill. Several of them make one trade.
FillPairOut.title: FillPairOut

ImportIssueOut.description: A line of the file that could not be used, numbered the way a spreadsheet numbers it.
ImportIssueOut.title: ImportIssueOut

ImportPreviewOut.description: What importing a file would do, worked out without saving anything. Mirrors `FileImportReport`.
ImportPreviewOut.title: ImportPreviewOut

NeighborsOut.description: The trades either side of one in the list the person came from; null at either end.
NeighborsOut.title: NeighborsOut

PreviewRowOut.description: One fill pair as the file states it: times are written the way the file writes them, in the CSV timezone.
PreviewRowOut.title: PreviewRowOut

SettingsPatch.description: Only the fields present change; `null` means the same as leaving the field out.
SettingsPatch.title: SettingsPatch

SummaryOut.description: Mirrors `finance.Summary`, plus how many accounts the trades came from.
SummaryOut.title: SummaryOut

TagEditIn.description: Rename, recolour or move a tag to another category: the whole tag, as it should now be.
TagEditIn.title: TagEditIn

UndoPreviewOut.description: What undoing an import removes (or, after the undo, removed). Mirrors `UndoReport`.
UndoPreviewOut.title: UndoPreviewOut

get.description: Every account with its progress against the firm's rules (closed trades only; see `api/progress.py`).
Every account, by name. Archived ones (passed, failed or closed) are included unless `include_archived=false`.

post.description: A new account with no rules and no fees yet (set those next).

put.description: Change an account's name, firm, type, size and starting balance. Changing the type reclassifies its trades.

post.description:
Mark an account as finished (an evaluation passes, fails or is closed; a funded account fails or is closed).
Its trades stay; views leave them out unless asked.

get.description: Dollars per contract, round trip, by contract root ("NQ"); `*` is the rate for any other contract.

delete.description: Remove a contract's own rate (it falls back to `*`). Stored trades are recalculated in the same change.

put.description: Set the rate for a contract root. The account's stored trades are recalculated in the same change.

get.description: The account's costs and payouts, oldest first.

post.description: Record money spent on the account (a fee) or received from it (a payout). The amount is always positive.

delete.description: Delete one entry and answer with what is left of the account's ledger.

put.description: Set the firm's rules (profit target, drawdown, trailing, daily loss limit). A rule left null is not tracked.

get.description: Across every account, archived ones included: what the accounts cost, what they paid out, how evaluations ended.
The headline numbers, equity curves, daily results, score and per-account results for the filtered trades.
Every import, newest first (undone ones included, marked).

post.description: Import the file into the account. Rows already stored are left alone, so importing a file twice is safe.

What importing this file into this account would do: counts, problems, and the first rows with a status each.
Nothing is saved (the import runs inside a transaction that is rolled back), so the preview is exactly what the
real import would do.
Remove what the import brought in (rows another import also holds stay) and regroup what is left.
What undoing the import would remove, without removing it.

delete.description: Delete a category, its tags, and those tags' links to trades (the trades themselves stay).

get.description: Every category and tag (each with the number of trades that carry it) and the colours on offer.

post.description: A new tag in a category, or the one already there under that name (any capitalization).

delete.description: Delete a tag everywhere, including from the trades that carry it.

put.description:
Rename, recolour or move a tag. The trades carrying it keep it; a name already used in the target category is
a conflict (merge the two instead).

post.description: Move every trade from this tag to another, then delete this one. A trade that carried both keeps one.

get.description: One page of the trade log, with the total count and net result of everything the filters match.
Everything about one trade. Another user's trade and a missing one are both a 404: they look the same.
The trades either side of this one in the list the person came from (same filters, search and order).

put.description: Replace a trade's notes. Answers with what was stored (a note with no visible text is stored as empty).

delete.description: Take a tag off a trade (not on it is fine); the tag stays for other trades. Answers with the trade's tags.

put.description: Put a tag on a trade (already there is fine). Answers with the trade's tags.
